debate.text: Rennowick expects about 120 early releases and has £480,000. Six supervisors see everyone within two days, and three liaison staff call victims. Answer A passed five of six. Three staff cannot promise every victim a call in 48 hours. The jury put check-ins first, 5 to 4. So this is a six-month trial to 24 May, and we publish every missed call. Feeling safe and being safe are different numbers.

Hollie, the first two days decide it. A man released with no address is back in front of a supervisor with nowhere to sleep. Aldmere's answer tied a bed to a named worker. Make the first visit about the key in the door, and I will make sure the council has one to hand.

And the pharmacy. Someone coming out on medication is out of tablets in a week. I have seen what that does in a ward. The supervisor should ask two things on day one: where are you sleeping, and have you got your tablets?

I will add a third. A job within a month is worth more than any check-in. But I will not pretend a supervisor can do that. It is for my trainee places and the Mereholt split. Hollie, send me the list, with names kept off it.

The jury asked for supervisors first, and the victims must not be left to wait in silence. I will publish the missed calls every quarter, the bad news included. The victims asked for a call. They should get a name and a number.

changes.text: A trial to 24 May 2027: six supervisors see everyone released early within two days, and three staff call victims, with every missed call published.
changes.why: Rennowick's answer A passed five of six tests and missed only the 48-hour victim calls, so it is a trial.
